The authors analyzed a sequence of JET plasmas with steady H-mode durations of ~5 s, all exhibiting intrinsic ELMing with no external ELM pacing.
ELM occurrence times were determined from the BeII signal, while the full flux loop signals VLD2 and VLD3 were used to extract the instantaneous phase.
The authors used the Hilbert transform to compute the analytic signal and determine the instantaneous phase of the VLD2 and VLD3 signals.
ELMs were found to occur preferentially when the full flux loop signals were at a specific phase, as shown in previous work by the authors.
In the 2-5 ms leading up to an ELM, the authors found that the phases of the VLD2 and VLD3 signals became progressively more aligned.
During this 2-5 ms build-up period, the VLD2 and VLD3 signals also became phase synchronized with each other.
The authors quantified the phase alignment using circular statistics, calculating the Rayleigh number R, standardized angular variance σ_φ, and p-value.
For δt < 5 ms before the ELM, the authors found R > 0.3 and small σ_φ, indicating significant phase alignment.
The authors tested the robustness of the ELM build-up signature by using Hilbert transform windows that stopped at the ELM time, in addition to those that extended beyond it.
The authors constructed surrogate time series to test the statistical significance of the observed phase alignments, confirming they were distinct from chance occurrence.
The authors suggest the ELM build-up signature, involving global synchronized plasma motion, is analogous to the global plasma perturbations that trigger ELMs in magnetically-kicked experiments.
The authors hypothesize that the intrinsic ELM burst follows a global plasma displacement that modifies conditions at the edge, leading to the onset of peeling-ballooning and other instabilities.
The authors' previous work found that intrinsic ELMs tend to occur preferentially at a specific phase of the full flux loop signals.
The current results build on this by showing the phases become progressively more aligned in the 2-5 ms leading up to the ELM.
This suggests a global, synchronized plasma response is part of the intrinsic ELM triggering process.
